name: Tesla, Inc.
thesis: Tesla trades at $373.18, down 1.23% intraday, with a market cap of $1.47T [1], but its valuation remains extremely elevated at a trailing P/E of 345.69x and a forward P/E of 174.0x [1]. Fiscal 2025 revenue of $94.83B declined 2.93% year-over-year, while net margin was thin at 4.0% and operating margin just 1.41%, with free cash flow of only $4.84B, indicating weakening core profitability despite a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1837 [1]. The stock's beta of 1.916 reflects high volatility, consistent with disclosed risks including production/ramp delays, lithium-ion cell and Gigafactory manufacturing issues, dependence on government incentives, supplier delivery risk, and explicitly acknowledged stock price volatility [2]. Given shrinking revenue, compressed margins, and a valuation pricing in substantial future growth, the current risk/reward appears unfavorable at these levels.
